content.text: I reviewed every payment, termination, and remedies provision. There is no Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee, or minimum-fee-on-termination anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: NO DAMAGES FOR TERMINATION. NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR DAMAGES OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, DAMAGES FOR THE LOSS OF GOODWILL, PROSPECTIVE PROFITS OR ANTICIPATED INCOME, OR DAMAGES RESULTING FROM ANY EXPENDITURES, INVESTMENTS, LEASES OR COMMITMENTS MADE BY EITHER PARTY ON ACCOUNT OF THE TERMINATION OR EXPIRATION OF THIS AGREEMENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH ITS TERMS.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee, or minimum-fee-on-termination payable by Licensee, so the preferred position ("Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties") is met. I checked the fee and payment articles (Article V user fees, Article VII support fee of $2,500/month, Supplemental Payments, tax gross-up), the term and termination provisions (Articles IV, XIX–XXI) and the remedies provisions (Articles XI, XIII, XXIII). Licensee's monetary obligations are all usage- or service-based consideration: on Licensor's termination for breach, Licensor retains only "the right to receive payments for all trades performed using the Licensed Technology" (p0049) — actual accrued fees, not a stipulated sum or acceleration of remaining contract value. Article XXIII (p0142) affirmatively bars termination-related damages of any kind against either party. Two provisions are cost-shifting rather than liquidated damages and are not flagged: Licensee bears audit cost if a discrepancy over 5% is found (p0064), and Licensee pays standard rates for out-of-scope error work (p0095). The rebate mechanic in p0076 runs in our favour. No redline proposed.
